identity.title: Align release platform precheck with the public sample catalog

origin.summary: The user approved proceeding with the recommended fix for the legacy platform precheck failure.

state.current_summary: The Dev precheck now accepts an explicit catalog path, release policy selects the public catalog, and the Windows PowerShell tutorial-term encoding failure is corrected. The current Dev public precheck passed; a clean reviewed candidate remains to be prepared separately.
state.next_action: Review the Dev diff, obtain separate commit authorization, then build and verify a clean candidate before any new tag or release action.

objective.summary: Make the release platform precheck reproducibly validate the repository-portable public sample contract while retaining the legacy catalog for explicit local historical checks.
constraints: Keep implementation and evidence in C:\Git\OpenVisionLab_Dev until original-repository promotion is explicitly authorized.
Do not reintroduce SDK or ignored Sample\... assets into public paths.
Retain the legacy catalog as an explicit local-only option rather than silently removing its coverage.
Do not modify, force-move, or republish the existing v2.1.0-rc.2 tag or draft as part of this change.
Keep commit, tag, tag push, release publication, and deployment as separate authorization stages.

criteria.text: RunVisionPlatformPrecheck.ps1 accepts and forwards CatalogPath, records the selected catalog in its evidence, and the release policy invokes the public catalog while documenting the legacy option.

A current Dev non-UI platform precheck using OpenVisionLab.PublicSampleCatalog.csv produces a top-level summary with Status=OK, all 13 gates OK, and public sample rows 33/33 with zero failures or metadata/artifact issues.
A clean reviewed candidate is rebuilt from the corrected source and passes the repository release gate before any new release tag or publication is considered.

milestones.summary: Add explicit public/legacy catalog routing and Windows PowerShell-safe tutorial term checks.
Run and retain a current Dev public-catalog platform precheck with complete top-level evidence.
Prepare and verify a clean candidate under separate release-stage authorization.
